prerequisites: Knowledge of the methods of analysis of the electric circuits in continuous and sinusoidal steady state.

learning_outcomes.text: Train the student's knowledge at a professional level to enable him to operate autonomously in the field of practical applications of electrical engineering such as: electrical machines and systems for powering these machines and other types of electrical users.
Application knowledge on electrical machines.
Use of Specific SW such as power line sizing programs.
Learning of operating principles of electrical machines for industrial use.
Learning of drives of electrical machines with electronic converters.
Learning of basics of improving the efficiency of industrial electrical equipment.
Learning of basics of sizing photovoltaic systems.
Advanced ability to conduct complex experiments and to manage instrumentation and advanced software.

Ability to analyze and model mechanical/electrical/propulsion components and systems: problems and models underlying industrial engineering, with particular reference to mechanical and energy engineering.
Advanced ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, procedures and methods, including the use of theoretical models, with awareness of their limitations and potential.
Ability to critically evaluate data and results and draw appropriate conclusions, being aware of the level of uncertainty that may affect them.
Ability to achieve preparation adequate for access to third-cycle studies (attendance at second-level masters and doctoral schools) to further deepen knowledge and skills in research.
Ability to analyze technologies of plants, components and processes and engineering methods and their economic implications.

Deep knowledge of the theoretical and scientific foundations of mathematics and other basic sciences to interpret and describe complex engineering problems or those requiring an interdisciplinary approach.
Knowledge and use of scientific tools (software and other instruments) specific to the design sector within the field of energy engineering.
Knowledge of methods to conceive, plan, design and manage complex and/or innovative systems, processes and services.
Knowledge of advanced design tools (mechanical, thermo-fluid-dynamic, electrical or multi-physics) for the modeling and numerical simulation of components or systems.
Knowledge of electric machines and their power systems for traction. Knowledge of the structural and thermo-fluid-dynamic aspects of internal combustion engines.
Knowledge of the main renewable energy sources and energy storage systems and of the criteria for their integration with conventional production systems.
A systemic knowledge of methodologies, technologies and applied aspects of electrical energy engineering.
Ability to independently analyze data and information, draw objective conclusions and make consequential decisions.
Ability to evaluate different options or solutions to a problem and to make informed decisions about oneís projects, including on the basis of relevant technical standards.
Ability to work in a coordinated group, with a clear understanding of the engineering problemís context and the interdisciplinary implications of the application area.

Autonomy in meeting commitments and deadlines, including the ability to allocate time and available resources to meet deadlines, to accurately assess oneís own capabilities and resources to ensure commitments are realistic and achievable, and to prioritize activities based on importance and timing.
Ability to identify the need for new knowledge.
Ability to communicate and transfer information, ideas, problems and solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Ability to present professionally problems, solutions, analyses and results through written reports and oral presentations.
Skills in graphical representation and communication (preparation of diagrams, charts and tables).
Ability for autonomous and continuous learning and professional updating in the relevant engineering field.
Conducting bibliographic research using major resources (libraries, scientific databases, etc.).
Project- and problem-based learning: ability to learn through teaching methods based on projects and on solving real problems.

syllabus_topics: Theoretical and operational introduction to electrical applications used in the industrial field such as: lighting systems and photovoltaic systems.
PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM DESIGN General aspects of photovoltaic systems.
Protection against direct and indirect contact.
Residual current circuit breakers, thermal circuit breakers, magnetic circuit breakers, circuit breakers, fuses, and surge arresters.
Monitoring of photovoltaic systems and performance verification.
Storage systems, grid connection, and cabin upgrades.
LIGHTING DESIGN AND EFFICIENCY Basic lighting concepts and related regulations.
Efficiency enhancement of lighting systems with LEDs.
Technical and economic examples of efficiency enhancement interventions for lighting systems.
Notes on legislation and CEI standards.
assessment_rules: The assessment includes intermediate tests consisting of exercises and an oral test evaluating communication skills and knowledge of course topics. For Electronic Engineering students, verification includes 'pen and paper' analysis of simple circuits, simulations using software, and practical laboratory activities (creation and testing of devices/prototypes). The final grade is based on a rubric from 'Fail' to 'Excellent or outstanding' (29-30 and Honors), where Honors is awarded for brilliance and originality exceeding expectations.
